cues: Its agile lead part often carries the melody in a brass quintet while lower voices supply harmony.
Rapid valve changes support sparkling runs, giving a dance-band lead its nimble character.
Military fanfares use its clear, carrying notes to announce commanders or mark formal arrivals.
At a jazz jam, its solo can trade short, bright phrases with a saxophone over a swinging rhythm.
An orchestral concerto gives the soloist room to display agile runs above the strings.
Bright, focused attacks make it effective for punctuating a big-band chart with emphatic accents.
